dataRole: primary-source-audited SGTE unary functions with the source magnetic contribution analytically expanded into the existing OBGEL temperature basis

referenceState.name: Standard Element Reference
referenceState.energyReference: H_SER(Fe), the enthalpy of Fe in its Standard Element Reference state

pressure.treatment: The temperature-only unary test omits Dinsdale's Gpres term. Dinsdale states that the pressure contribution can be ignored for applications at low or moderate pressure.

sourceToRepositoryPhaseNames.identityNote: One crystallographic phase across the full modeled interval; the Curie point is not a phase-key boundary.

scope.hcpInclusionRationale: Dinsdale explicitly supplies an HCP_A3 Fe function. Although HCP is not stable on the computed 1 bar lower envelope, retaining it is scientifically useful as an audited allotrope candidate and verifies that the reader does not promote a high-pressure-relevant phase at the fixed ambient pressure.

systemValidity.rationale: The interval follows the common 298.15-6000 K range printed by Dinsdale (1991) for the temperature-only BCC_A2, FCC_A1, HCP_A3, and LIQUID Fe functions. OBGEL evaluates the finite limiting values at the two endpoints as the closed canonical domain and does not extrapolate beyond it.

mathematicalConventions.segmentIntervals: Endpoint inclusion is explicit. Adjacent source or magnetic branches are lower-inclusive and upper-exclusive; final branches are upper-inclusive.
mathematicalConventions.outsideValidity: No canonical value is supplied outside systemValidity; consumer-level extrapolation must be explicit.
mathematicalConventions.coefficientInterpretation: Each function evaluates to J/mol when T is supplied in K.
mathematicalConventions.baseFunctionSemantics: No baseFunction is used in this entry. Every phase is encoded directly as its absolute G-H_SER expression so the generic reader can compare phase-identity keys without magnetic-reference cancellation.

magneticContribution.sourceAttribution: Dinsdale attributes the definition to Hillert and Jarl following Inden.
magneticContribution.expandedBasisStrategy: Multiplication by T converts the low branch to constant, T, T^4, T^10, and T^16 terms and the high branch to T^-4, T^-14, and T^-24 terms. These coefficients are added to the corresponding nonmagnetic source segment.
magneticContribution.phaseIdentityRule: The 1043 K branch boundary changes only the magnetic expression. Both sides remain the single bcc phase function.

magneticContribution.sourceAttribution: Dinsdale attributes the definition to Hillert and Jarl following Inden.
magneticContribution.unexpandedSourceRelationship: The same Dinsdale Hillert-Jarl/Inden relationship used for BCC applies with Tstar = TN = 67 K, beta0 = 0.7, and p = 0.28.
magneticContribution.expandedBasisStrategy: Because all of systemValidity is above 67 K, only the tau > 1 branch is needed; multiplication by T gives T^-4, T^-14, and T^-24 terms added to both source FCC segments.

modelConstruction.phaseIdentityDecision: The functions object is keyed by phase identity. BCC-A2 is represented by the single key bcc throughout systemValidity. Ferromagnetic and paramagnetic states are not separate phases.
modelConstruction.magneticCompatibilityDecision: The generic reader is unchanged. Magnetic Gibbs energies are analytically expanded into ordinary temperaturePower terms in each applicable temperature segment.
modelConstruction.physicalModelPreservation: The unexpanded Hillert-Jarl/Inden relationship and all Dinsdale Fe magnetic parameters are retained in phase metadata so the expanded coefficients remain traceable to the physical contribution.

extensions.statement: Every candidate function is supplied by Dinsdale over the complete systemValidity interval; no mathematical extension is encoded and no extrapolation is permitted outside systemValidity.

modelConstruction.pressureTreatment: Gpres is not encoded for this fixed 1 bar unary test, following Dinsdale's statement that the pressure contribution can be ignored for low or moderate pressures.

sourceOfDinsdaleIronAssessment.citationAsPrinted: A. Fernandez Guillermet and P. Gustafson, High Temperatures-High Pressures, 1985, 16, 591-610
sourceOfDinsdaleIronAssessment.role: Dinsdale's stated underlying source for the four retained Fe phase assessments; the canonical coefficients are transcribed from Dinsdale (1991).

sourceProvenance.provenanceRule: The numerical functions and transition constraints in this entry are tied specifically to the inspected Dinsdale (1991) reproduction. Later SGTE database revisions are not silently substituted.

verification.reproducibilityRule: All computed values are consequences of the encoded functions and are not model inputs.

implementation.note: The source writes R symbolically; 8.31451 J/(mol K), the SGTE-era conventional value, is recorded explicitly so the expanded representation is reproducible.

sourceExpressionEquivalence.bcc: Each expanded magnetic branch was obtained by Expand of the recorded source relationship after substituting Tstar, beta0, p, D, and R, then added termwise to the source BCC expression.
sourceExpressionEquivalence.fcc: The tau > 1 magnetic branch was expanded and added termwise to both FCC source expressions; TN = 67 K is outside systemValidity.
sourceExpressionEquivalence.condition: encoded phase expression equals Dinsdale nonmagnetic expression plus the unexpanded Gmag expression on every applicable segment

stableEnvelope.hcpResult: HCP is never the minimum-Gibbs-energy phase over systemValidity at 1 bar.
stableEnvelope.reentrantPhaseResult: The same bcc phase key and the same BCC Gibbs function are stable below the FCC region and again above it; no separate alpha-BCC and delta-BCC phase identities are introduced.

unchangedReaderValidation.resultType: derived implementation validation; not an independent thermodynamic prediction
unchangedReaderValidation.sourceComparisonRule: Dinsdale/SGTE transition-table temperatures are audited authoritative assessment constraints. The reader results and numerical equality roots are consequences of the encoded functions and must not be described as independent predictions.

stableEnvelopeTransitions.precisionNote: Retained exactly as reported by the completed reader run.

unchangedReaderValidation.phaseIdentity: One bcc phase identity is retained. Its re-entrant stability is recovered with the same BCC Gibbs function stable below the FCC interval and again above it.
unchangedReaderValidation.magneticOrderingResult: The 1043 K BCC Curie transition remains an internal magnetic-ordering contribution to the BCC Gibbs function and is not reported as a crystallographic stable-envelope transition.
unchangedReaderValidation.representationResult: The Hillert-Jarl/Inden magnetic contribution is expanded into ordinary OBGEL basis terms for compatibility with the unchanged reader while its physical magnetic parameters, unexpanded relationship, and provenance remain recorded. A future first-class contributions mechanism remains deferred architecture, not a current reader requirement.
